title: Simple, Robust, Scalable Semi-supervised Learning via Expectation Regularization
authors: Gideon S. Mann and Andrew McCallum
venue: Proceedings of the 24th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2007)
conclusions: Introduces expectation regularization (XR): augments the conditional log-likelihood objective for exponential-family models (e.g. logistic regression / MaxEnt) with a KL-divergence term that pulls the model's expected conditional probabilities on UNLABELED data toward designer-provided expectations (e.g. label priors).

Special case 'label regularization': the designer supplies a target marginal label distribution p-tilde(y), and XR encourages the model's average predicted label distribution over unlabeled data to match it -- a SOFT, aggregate/global penalty, not a hard per-instance or per-count constraint.

Empirically evaluated on 5 datasets (SRAA, POS, SecStr, BIOII, CoNLL03) against 7 supervised/semi-supervised baselines (naive Bayes, SVM, EM, MaxEnt, entropy regularization, cluster kernels, graph-based QC); XR wins or is competitive in nearly all settings and is especially strong with very little labeled data.

Shown to be robust to substantial noise in the provided label-prior estimates (majority-class probability corrupted from 84% down to ~11% before performance degrades) and robust across a wide range of the lambda/temperature meta-parameters.
Positions XR as simpler/cheaper than TSVMs, entropy regularization, and graph-based methods (no pre-clustering, no auxiliary functions, scales linearly in number of unlabeled points).
Does not enforce any hard cap/quota on class counts and is not framed as a constrained-optimization method with multipliers; it is a soft regularization term added to the likelihood.
